sections.text: Dollar index 101.76 (+0.3% in a month, +3.5% YTD). USD/BRL 5.436 (+4.5% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.652 (-0.8%); USD/MXN 18.91 (+4.8%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.text: WTI 104.00 $/bbl (+17.6% in a month), Brent 113.22, ULSD 4.684 $/gal (+3.9%), natural gas 2.86 (-15.0%). us_econ: Inflation: CPI 3.7% y/y (2026-09), core 2.6%; core 3-month annualized 3.4%; core PCE 3.0%. Jobs: payrolls +29k in 2026-09 (3-month average +51k), unemployment 4.2% (+0.1), wages 3.0% y/y. Growth: real GDP 2.2% annualized in 2026-Q2, consumer spending 3.8%. Policy: fed funds target 3.75-4.0% (effective 3.88%); 2-year Treasury 4.61% (+0.73 vs fed funds: market pricing hikes); 10-year breakeven inflation 2.35%, real 10-year 2.63%. Farm prices (PPI farm products) +1.5% y/y; food-at-home CPI +1.8% y/y. For ags: high real yields and a firm dollar weigh on fund demand for commodities; sticky inflation keeps rates high (carry and storage costs up); a weak job market or falling real incomes hits meat and dairy demand first.
